hed: The Dam Is Quiet. The Trout Will Eat.
deck: Table Rock 909.55 ft. 20 cfs through the dam at 12:00 CT. Taneycomo still eats a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Warm the hands, not the water.
play.body: Fish the warmest part of the afternoon on the lake. Fish first light on the trout water. Different climates.

season.name: Winter trout
season.why: Table Rock gets quiet and vertical. Taneycomo becomes the reason you came. This is Johnny Morris water — cold, clear, and honest.
tips: Spoon or ice jig over 30–50 feet on Table Rock if you must. Most people shouldn't.
Taneycomo is the trip: midges, eggs, pink worms, tiny jigs, 2-pound test.
Generation still rules. A winter blowdown is a drift day.
Felt soles and a staff if you wad. The rocks don't care that you're on vacation.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new USACE level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 909.93 early in the week to 909.55 this morning — about 0.38 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Live USACE reading 12:00 CT: 909.55 ft, 20 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — we do not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: Table Rock sits at 909.55 ft this morning — a live USACE number, not a guess. Full pool is 915. Heat and a falling or hanging pool put bass on main-lake points, gravel, brush, and the first good humps in 15 to 35 feet. If you don't have electronics, you are guessing at bait.

Generation at the dam right now is 20 cfs (turbine 20). Overnight it backed off to about 20; the afternoon peak on this sheet hit 20. That pattern — quiet early, lean on it later — is the late-summer White River book.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~20 cfs at 12:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: Below Table Rock Dam this is a trout river that happens to be called a lake. The water comes out of the bottom cold and gin-clear. The generators decide whether you wade or drift.

Last printed reading: 20 cfs at 12:00 CT. We will not invent the next hour. Southwestern Power keeps the live sheet. The number is 866-494-1993. Call it in the parking lot. Off or near-off: pink Power Worm, wade, kids. Two-thousand-plus: dock or boat, fish the seams.
Light line — two to six pound. Rainbows are most of the creel. Slot in the upper water: put the 12-to-20-inch rainbows back. Don't horse them in this clarity. Don't wad a rising tailrace.

editor.note: Always-on desk: live USACE Little Rock gage (tabrock.htm) plus seasonal playbook. Today's Mac scout was on file. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
